questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best medication treatment for premature ejaculation?
questions.explanation: SSRIs have been shown to be a good treatment for premature ejaculation, with paroxetine being the medication that delays ejaculation the most.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia is hospitalized and treated with haloperidol and benztropine. The patient becomes distressed, has a temperature of 103°F and has labile blood pressure. Physical examination reveals hypertonicity, diaphoresis, and tachycardia. Laboratory studies reveal a creatine kinase of 55,000 IU/L. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Essential for the diagnosis of neuroleptic malignant syndrome in a patient on antipsychotic medication are rigidity and elevated temperature. Two or more of the following symptoms are also required: diaphoresis, tachycardia, elevated or labile blood pressure, dysphagia, incontinence, tremor, changes in the level of consciousness ranging from confusion to coma, mutism, leukocytosis, laboratory evidence of muscle injury (e.g., elevated creatine kinase).

questions.question_text: A female patient reveals during a psychotherapy session that she does not enjoy sexual intercourse. She states that she is aroused by her partner but has sharp pains throughout intercourse. She cannot relax and enjoy sex and has begun to avoid sex because of the anticipation of the pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Sexual pain disorders are not a common chief complaint in mental health settings. However, during psychotherapy a psychiatrist may become aware of the symptoms and should be able to recognize them. This is a classic description of dyspareunia.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old woman presents with severe anxiety after finding out that her biological mother was recently diagnosed with Huntington's disease. There is no family history of the disease on her father's side. She wishes to know if she is affected. The probability that she is affected is:
questions.explanation: Huntington's disease is inherited by an autosomal dominant transmission. With one affected parent and one unaffected parent, by chance, one could expect 50% of offspring would be affected and 50% unaffected but each individual child has a 50% chance of developing the disease.

questions.question_text: A 9-year-old boy is referred for evaluation because he is having 'temper tantrums' in school. He cannot sit still, constantly disrupts the class, runs out in the hall without permission and refuses to obey directives from the teacher. He frequently fights with his peers, and if he does not get what he wants, he yells, screams, throws objects, and flails about on the floor. Educational testing reveals borderline intellectual functioning and significant delays in reading, writing, spelling, and mathematics. On physical examination, the boy is noted to be in the fifth percentile for head circumference. He has short palpebral fissures, a thin upper lip, and a smooth philtrum. The boy was most likely exposed to which of the following drugs in utero?
questions.explanation: The teratological effects of prenatal alcohol exposure have been well studied and are described by fetal alcohol syndrome. Alcohol is a direct neuroteratogen that affects not only fetal facial morphology and growth but also brain growth, structure, and function. As a result, children exposed to alcohol have an unusually high prevalence of intellectual impairment and disruptive behavior disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most accurate statement regarding psychotherapy for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)?

options.text: The therapist should be as nondirective as possible for the psychotherapy to be effective.
Multiple modalities of psychotherapy have proven effective for PTSD.
Psychotherapy must be combined with pharmacotherapy to be effective.
Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is of little value for patients with PTSD.

correct_answer.text: Multiple modalities of psychotherapy have proven effective for PTSD.

correct_answers.text: Multiple modalities of psychotherapy have proven effective for PTSD.

questions.explanation: In meta-analyses of controlled trials of psychological treatments of PTSD, multiple forms of psychotherapy, including exposure therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, and psychodynamic therapy, have been shown to be effective.

questions.question_text: A husband and wife present for treatment because the wife is concerned. Her husband recently told her that he believes he was born a woman. He states that he has always felt this way but can't fight it anymore. He has started wearing dresses around the house after he arrives home from work at the end of the day. He says that he loves his wife and kids but that he needs to be happy as well. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This is a complicated disorder, but the scenario describes someone who has been struggling with gender identity disorder despite functioning in culturally expected roles for a prolonged period.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the pharmacokinetics of children younger than 12 years old?

options.text: Children absorb medications more slowly than adults.
Children metabolize through hepatic pathways more slowly than adults.
Children have a smaller volume of distribution than adults.
Children have more efficient renal function than adults.

correct_answer.text: Children have more efficient renal function than adults.

correct_answers.text: Children have more efficient renal function than adults.

questions.explanation: Children have more efficient renal elimination than adults and therefore will clear drugs using this pathway more quickly.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old woman develops anorgasmia while taking paroxetine. Switching to which of the following medications is most likely to resolve this problem?
questions.explanation: A large survey of primary care clinics found that sexual dysfunction is substantially less common with bupropion compared to other SSRIs.

questions.question_text: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents with the chief complaint that 'he keeps having nightmares.' His parents report that for the past month, during the first one-third of the night, the boy awakens from his sleep with a startled scream. When they enter the room, they find that he has broken out in a sweat, is difficult to awaken, and looks 'scared to death.' The next morning he has no recall of the event. These episodes are most likely occurring during which stage of sleep?
questions.explanation: Sleep terror disorder is a parasomnia. It occurs in deep non-REM (i.e., stages 3 or 4) sleep. This stage of sleep occurs predominantly in the first third of the night.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common psychiatric disturbance among adolescents who die by suicide?
questions.explanation: Approximately one-half to two-thirds of adolescent suicide victims have a depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: A previously well 24-year-old woman presented with a 4-week history of progressively worsening expansive irritable mood, pressured speech, racing thoughts, grandiosity, and distractibility. More recently she heard the voice of God proclaiming her to be a special messenger. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Brief psychotic disorder without marked stressor

questions.explanation: The patient meets DSM-IV-TR criteria for a manic episode with mood-congruent auditory hallucinations. The psychotic symptoms occurring only in the context of a manic episode make the other diagnoses unlikely.

questions.question_text: According to the principles of dialectical behavior therapy, the core deficit in borderline personality disorder is:
questions.explanation: Dialectical behavior therapy is based on the theory that line symptoms primarily reflect dysfunction of the emotion regulation system.

questions.question_text: According to the American Psychiatric Association guidelines, which of the following is true regarding a psychiatrist engaging in a sexual relationship with a former patient?

options.text: Acceptable provided at least 5 years have passed since the termination of the doctor-patient relationship
Acceptable provided at least 2 years have passed since the termination of the doctor-patient relationship
Acceptable provided the former patient initiates the relationship and it is clear to both parties that no exploitation is taking place
Unethical no matter how long it has been since the termination of the doctor-patient relationship

correct_answer.text: Unethical no matter how long it has been since the termination of the doctor-patient relationship

correct_answers.text: Unethical no matter how long it has been since the termination of the doctor-patient relationship

questions.explanation: While the issue of sexual relationships with former patients is not without controversy, psychiatrists should be aware of the current position of the American Psychiatric Association, which forbids sex with former patients.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia begins treatment with clozapine. The baseline white blood cell count (WBC) is 8100 (normal=4500-11,000/mm3). The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is 6200 (normal=1500-8000/mm%). The tests remain normal in weekly monitoring. After 3 months, the patient has had significant clinical improvement, but the WBC drops to 3200, the ANC drops to 2100, and immature cell forms are present on peripheral blood smear. Repeat tests show a WBC of 3100, an ANC of 1900, and no immature cell forms. The physical examination is normal, with no fever, sore throat, or other sign of infection. What would be the best next step in the management of this patient?

options.text: Reduce the dose of clozapine and begin weekly monitoring of the WBC and differential.
Routinely monitor the WBC and differential unless the patient develops signs and symptoms of infection.
Interrupt clozapine therapy until the WBC is normal, and then resume treatment.
Continue current dosage of clozapine and begin twice-weekly monitoring of the WBC and differential.

correct_answer.text: Continue current dosage of clozapine and begin twice-weekly monitoring of the WBC and differential.

correct_answers.text: Continue current dosage of clozapine and begin twice-weekly monitoring of the WBC and differential.

questions.explanation: A protocol has been established for monitoring the hematologic effects of clozapine. In this vignette, the patient's WBC and ANC have dropped from baseline, but the patient has demonstrated an excellent response to medication and has no signs or symptoms of infection.

questions.question_text: According to DSM-IV-TR, which personality disorder cannot be diagnosed in children and adolescents?
questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder cannot be diagnosed in individuals under the age of 18 years. The other personality disorders can be diagnosed if the maladaptive personality traits are pervasive, persistent, and unlikely to be limited to a particular developmental stage or episode of an axis I disorder.

questions.question_text: The first-line treatment of choice (determined by expert consensus) for acute posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) milder severity is:

options.text: combination of a mood stabilizer and psychotherapy.

questions.explanation: The expert panel felt that for milder severity acute PTSD, psychotherapy first was the treatment of choice.

questions.question_text: A 54-year-old woman is hospitalized with hyperthermia, myoclonus, delirium, and autonomic instability. Which of the following medication combinations would be most likely to cause this clinical presentation?
questions.explanation: The patient's symptoms are consistent with a serotonin syndrome. Monoamine oxidase inhibitors, such as phenelzine, combined with serotonergic antidepressants pose a grave risk; hence, such combinations are contraindicated.

questions.question_text: In addition to lithium, which of the following is recommended as a first line monotherapy for bipolar disorder, depressed mood, in the revised APA Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Bipolar Disorder (2002)?
questions.explanation: The Practice Guideline recommends the initiation of treatment of bipolar depression with lithium or lamotrigine and states that traditional antidepressants are not recommended given the risk of precipitating a switch into mania.

questions.question_text: A 15-year-old African American male high school freshman is referred to a psychiatrist because of increasing oppositional behavior at school. In middle school he was an honor roll student, played soccer, and was on student council, all of which he continued in his first 9 weeks of high school. On the weekends, he volunteers at a local Boys and Girls Club and plays the keyboard at his church. After a couple of sessions, he finally admits that he needed to 'prove myself to my boys because they said I was 'acting white.' Which of the following is the most likely reason for his peers' denigration?
questions.explanation: A subset of African American culture that particularly affects male adolescents devalues academic performance and emphasizes aggressive and 'street' behavior.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old man presents with depressed mood, poor concentration, poor appetite, feelings of worthlessness, and insomnia 4 weeks after alcohol cessation. There is no history of mania. Which of the following is the best next step?
questions.explanation: The patient has symptoms of a major depressive episode that have persisted for 2 weeks. Rather than addressing insomnia as a symptom in isolation, it is preferable to begin treatment for the depressive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 16-year-old girl with depression has suicidal ideation. Which of the following characteristics is the most strongly associated with a greater risk of completed suicide?
questions.explanation: A previous suicide attempt is the most potent predictor of suicide in girls.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist routinely receives free golf outings, concert tickets, and dinners as gifts from a local pharmaceutical representative. Which of the following statements most adequately describes the ethics of this practice?

options.text: This is a conflict of interest for the psychiatrist.
There is no evidence that pharmaceutical company marketing to physicians influences physicians' behavior.
Self-monitoring and self-regulation are the most effective ways of minimizing harm from conflicts of interest.
It is ethical if no single gift is worth more than $250.

correct_answer.text: This is a conflict of interest for the psychiatrist.

correct_answers.text: This is a conflict of interest for the psychiatrist.

questions.explanation: Self-monitoring and self-regulation actions by the psychiatrist are important but usually are not seen as sufficient to prevent abuse due to conflicts of interest.

questions.question_text: The process of gene mapping, performed to determine whether or not a particular allele occurs more frequently than by chance in affected individuals, is known as which type of study?
questions.explanation: Association studies can examine whether a particular allele occurs more frequently than by chance by comparing affected and unaffected individuals.

questions.question_text: The highest rates of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) have been reported to be induced by:
questions.explanation: Assaultive violence, including sexual assault, produces the highest rates of PTSD, compared with other precipitating traumas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following laboratory test results is elevated in some patients with anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Values for the other tests are often decreased in patients with anorexia nervosa.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common side effect of cholinesterase inhibitors?
questions.explanation: Nausea, reported in 11%-47% of patients, is the most common adverse effect of the cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine).

questions.question_text: There is accumulating evidence suggesting that all of the following psychotherapies are beneficial in bipolar | disorder EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: There is peer-reviewed evidence suggesting that interpersonal and social rhythm therapy, family therapy, and cognitive behavioral therapy may decrease cycling and decrease the severity of bipolar | disorder. There are no controlled studies demonstrating that psychoanalysis decreases the frequency or severity of episodes of mania or depression.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old patient with heroin dependence is admitted to the infectious disease service for intravenous antibiotic treatment of bacterial endocarditis. An HIV test is negative. There is no other past psychiatric history. Opiate withdrawal is adequately controlled with oral methadone. On hospital day 3, the patient becomes acutely anxious, has moderate tachycardia, and asks to be discharged from the hospital. A low-grade fever develops, but blood cultures are negative and a complete blood count shows no significant increase or shift in leukocytes. The most likely explanation for the change in the patient's condition is:

options.text: a medication reaction, most likely to the antibiotic.

questions.explanation: The patient's tachycardia and symptoms of anxiety are consistent with the time frame for alcohol or sedative-hypnotic withdrawal.

questions.question_text: Long-term treatment with which of the following medications has been demonstrated to reduce suicide risk in bipolar disorder?
questions.explanation: Analyses of the results of many studies support a marked reduction in suicide rates and suicide attempts during long-term lithium treatment.

questions.question_text: A psychiatric referral is requested to evaluate a 25-year-old woman who wishes to undergo a second rhinoplasty because, she states, 'the first one left my nose too big.' In tears, the patient states that her discomfort about the appearance of her nose prevents her from having an active social life. She pleads with the psychiatrist to render an opinion that will permit the surgery. The patient does not appear, psychotic. She does not express any other obsessional thoughts. In the psychiatrist's opinion, the patient's nose is unremarkable. Which of the following disorders is the most likely diagnosis for this patient?
questions.explanation: This patient demonstrates the diagnostic criteria for body dysmorphic disorder. She is preoccupied with a perceived defect in her appearance, and this concern affects her adaptation socially.

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old man is treated with several trials of single antidepressants. His unipolar depression has been only partially responsive. Which of the following agents has the best evidence from randomized controlled trials to support its use in augmenting his antidepressant?
questions.explanation: Lithium is the best studied augmentation agent in the treatment of unipolar depression.

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old man seen in the emergency department is agitated, tachycardic, hypertensive, and tremulous. He sees fish swimming on the wall: 'It's just like watching television.' The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Visual hallucinations suggest the need to rule out an organic cause related to delirium.

questions.question_text: A 42-year-old morbidly obese man is seen for chronic fatigue. Findings on polysomnography indicate obstructive sleep apnea. If the sleep apnea is left untreated over a prolonged period, which of the following conditions is most likely to develop?
questions.explanation: Long-standing sleep apnea is associated with increased pulmonary blood flow and eventually increased systemic blood pressure as well.

questions.question_text: A patient in psychotherapy believes that her therapist wants to help her, she characteristically trusts him with very private material, and she has at times expressed her feeling that they have many things in common and that in many ways she views him as a role model. This patient's alliance is best characterized as:
questions.explanation: It is important to recognize an 'average expectable' positive transference and not to confuse it with other transference configurations.

questions.question_text: For which of the anxiety disorders does clonazepam have an FDA indication?
questions.explanation: Although clonazepam is often used as a general anxiolytic, its only FDA indications are seizure disorders and panic disorder.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old female presents with symptoms of depression. She is always thinking that the worst will occur in her relationships and employment, and she feels powerless to alter or control these events. She is seeking treatment with a therapist who provides cognitive behavior therapy. What is the most likely focus of the therapy for this patient?
questions.explanation: Depression in cognitive behavior therapy is defined as resulting from maladaptive thought patterns.

questions.question_text: Which medication is most effective in treating atypical depression?
questions.explanation: The available data indicate that monoamine oxidase inhibitors are more effective than tricyclic antidepressants for atypical depression.

questions.question_text: 'Guevodoces,' which translates as 'penis at 12,' refers to Dominican children with a female appearance at birth, reared as girls, who at puberty develop male secondary sexual characteristics and male-typical sexual urges and behaviors. The genetic condition they have is called:
questions.explanation: 5-alpha reductase is the enzyme that converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the hormone necessary for fetal masculinization.

questions.question_text: Rapid cycling is LEAST likely to respond to:
questions.explanation: Haloperidol, a conventional antipsychotic, has no indication for the treatment of the rapid cycling subtype of bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: During a follow-up visit, a 10-year-old woman with schizophrenia reports no improvement in her symptoms despite being on an appropriate dose of an antipsychotic medication for 3 weeks. The most reasonable initial approach would be to:

options.text: increase the dose of the patient's current medication.

questions.explanation: Poor adherence with the antipsychotic medication regimen is a common reason for lack of improvement.

questions.question_text: A small-town newspaper's reporter calls a psychiatrist to get 'a professional's opinion' on the publicized misbehavior of the district's elected representative, who may or may not have bipolar disorder. The reporter asks the psychiatrist, who has never met the representative, 'Why do you think the representative misbehaved, doctor?' The psychiatrist's ethical obligations would lead to which of the following responses?

options.text: Comment on the general nature of psychiatric illnesses.
Comment on the representative's condition only if the representative has not been a patient.

Comment on either childhood dynamic origins or brain abnormality as the possible cause of the representative's problems, if public records contain information that is consistent with such possibilities.
Inform the public about the representative's bipolar disorder, since this person is a public figure.

correct_answer.text: Comment on the general nature of psychiatric illnesses.

correct_answers.text: Comment on the general nature of psychiatric illnesses.

questions.explanation: A psychiatrist may comment on the general nature of psychiatric illnesses. However, it is unethical for a psychiatrist to publicly render a professional opinion about a person who is not the psychiatrist's own patient, who has not been properly examined by the psychiatrist, and who has not given proper informed consent to the psychiatrist to disclose professional opinions.

questions.question_text: In psychodynamic psychotherapy, a boundary crossing—unlike a boundary violation—is:

options.text: an exploitative break in the therapeutic frame.
generally not examined in the therapy.

questions.explanation: A boundary crossing is typically a benign and even helpful break in the therapeutic frame, especially when it is discussed in the therapy and the countertransference action leads to further exploration of the transference.

questions.question_text: A male psychiatrist has been conducting weekly psychotherapy for the last 4 months with a female patient. The patient has serious financial problems due to overspending. One day, the patient brings in a gift-wrapped box to the session and, handing the box to the psychiatrist, blurts out, 'It's a $100 tie ... I couldn't help myself, it just looked like something you'd wear and I'm so grateful for all of your help. Please accept it!' Which of the following is an appropriate response for the psychiatrist to give to this patient?

options.text: Accept the gift but donate it to charity without telling the patient.
Accept the gift but make it clear that the psychiatrist is uncomfortable doing so, given the patient's financial difficulties.
Acknowledge the patient's gratitude, discuss the implications, but state that as a general policy the psychiatrist does not accept gifts from patients.
Decline the gift without further explanation.

correct_answer.text: Acknowledge the patient's gratitude, discuss the implications, but state that as a general policy the psychiatrist does not accept gifts from patients.

correct_answers.text: Acknowledge the patient's gratitude, discuss the implications, but state that as a general policy the psychiatrist does not accept gifts from patients.

questions.explanation: While accepting small gifts from patients may be ethically acceptable at times, in the scenario in this question, accepting the tie is probably unethical for several reasons.

questions.question_text: A consultation is requested for a 16-year-old male who has been in detention for the past 2 months on charges of possession of cocaine. The detention center staff describe the youth as hyperactive, inattentive, impulsive, and easily distracted. A review of his educational history indicates that the youth has been in special education classes since the first grade because of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and a mixed expressive-receptive language disorder. On examination, there is no evidence of a mood or anxiety disorder or current substance abuse. Which of the following medications would be most appropriate for this patient?
questions.explanation: Atomoxetine is a recently approved nonstimulant medication for the treatment of ADHD. The drug is effective in patients with a history of substance abuse.

questions.question_text: A 78-year-old patient with major depressive disorder is being treated with atorvastatin and metoprolol for cardiovascular disease. Which of the following antidepressants is best used with these two other medications?
questions.explanation: Escitalopram has no clinically meaningful P450 inhibitory effects, although it can cause a minor increase in metoprolol levels. Inhibition of 3A4 by nefazodone could substantially increase atorvastatin blood levels and increase the risk of side effects.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old woman presents to the clinic with a chief complaint of having sexual problems. She reports that she gets aroused and enjoys intercourse but is unable to have an orgasm. She believes the problem started about a month ago, when her physician prescribed a medication for her 'anxiety attacks.' The medication was most likely:
questions.explanation: Sexual side effects are the most common adverse effect of SSRIs, with an incidence between 50% and 80%. The most common complaints are inhibited orgasm and decreased libido.

questions.question_text: Methylphenidate has its greatest action on which of the following neurotransmitter systems?
questions.explanation: Methylphenidate's mechanism of action is believed to lie in dopamine presynaptic release and reuptake blockade.

questions.question_text: Which mental disorder is the most frequent cause of first-onset psychosis after age 60?
questions.explanation: Several epidemiological studies have established dementia of the Alzheimer's type as the most common cause of late-life psychosis.

questions.question_text: Psychotic features do NOT occur during which of the following?
questions.explanation: DSM-IV-TR criterion E for hypomanic episode includes '...and there are no psychotic features.' Psychotic features can be associated with manic, mixed, and major depressive episodes.

questions.question_text: The parents of a 7-year-old boy express concern about his bed-wetting. The boy seems well-adjusted, and the family has developed a nonstigmatizing system to care for his bed and personal hygiene. He has no medical problems. After explaining the natural history of enuresis, the most reasonable initial approach would be to:
questions.explanation: The natural history of enuresis is that a substantial number of children remit after age 7. Given that the boy appears to be doing well, a reasonable approach is to wait and see if the enuresis improves with age.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist repeatedly and increasingly fantasizes about a sexual relationship with a patient in psychotherapy whom the psychiatrist finds very attractive. The psychiatrist is considering the possibility that the prohibition of sex with patients may not apply in this case because of some extenuating circumstances. Which of the following options would be the most ethical behavior on the part of the psychiatrist?

options.text: Because there are important psychodynamic therapeutic implications for the patient, share the fantasies with the patient if the benefits seem to outweigh the risks.
Transfer the patient's care to another psychiatrist.
Increase the frequency of therapy sessions in order to make the best use of the intensity of the transference that is developing.
Keep a diary of the sexual fantasies in order to contain them.

correct_answer.text: Transfer the patient's care to another psychiatrist.

correct_answers.text: Transfer the patient's care to another psychiatrist.

questions.explanation: While termination of psychotherapy is a dramatic step, it is the best choice among the four options in preserving the patient's welfare.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about a defendant's competency to stand trial for a criminal offense is NOT correct?

options.text: The defendant must be able to remember what he or she was doing at the time of the offense.
The defendant must be able to understand basic courtroom procedure.
The defendant must be able to understand the nature of various possible pleas and their consequences.
The defendant must be able to communicate with attorneys.

correct_answer.text: The defendant must be able to remember what he or she was doing at the time of the offense.

correct_answers.text: The defendant must be able to remember what he or she was doing at the time of the offense.

questions.explanation: Amnesia for the time of the offense usually does not interfere with the defendant's ability to consult with the attorney(s) and construct a valid defense unless the amnesia is part of an ongoing mental process such as dementia.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old Puerto Rican woman presents in distress at the outpatient clinic. She reports that her grandfather recently died, and since then she has been afflicted by several bouts of 'ataque de nervios.' She has these spells only when she is upset. A detailed history should be obtained to distinguish ataque from which other axis I diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Symptoms of ataque de nervios include uncontrollable shouting, attacks of crying, trembling, a sense of heat in the chest that migrates to the head, and verbal and physical aggression, some of which overlap with panic disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following signs or symptoms alone would be sufficient to meet criterion A for the active phase of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: In order to meet criterion A for schizophrenia, there has to be at least 1 month of symptoms, or less if successfully treated. The symptoms are one of five items: delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized or catatonic behavior, and negative symptoms.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old woman was unexpectedly terminated from her job. Two months later she presents tearfully with depressed mood and occasional feelings of hopelessness; she still feels stressed by the loss of her job. She has no prior history of depression, is not suicidal, has not had changes in appetite, weight, sleep, or energy level, and still gets pleasure from family and hobbies. Which of the following diagnoses would be the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Her symptoms developed in response to an identifiable stressor and appeared within 3 months of the stressor. The symptoms do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of alcohol dependence?
questions.explanation: In 1995 the FDA approved naltrexone, an opioid antagonist, for the treatment of alcohol dependence.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist maintains private therapy progress notes, in addition to medical record notes, that contain extremely sensitive clinical information. This practice is:

options.text: not acceptable, because the risks to the patient outweigh the benefits.
not acceptable, because all clinical material should be included in patients' medical records.
an acceptable way of preventing court-mandated access to sensitive clinical information.
an acceptable means of enhancing patient confidentiality.

correct_answer.text: an acceptable means of enhancing patient confidentiality.

correct_answers.text: an acceptable means of enhancing patient confidentiality.

questions.explanation: Private progress notes can be a useful tool for protecting patient confidentiality, since there is value in maintaining more detailed therapy notes for patient care as well as for teaching purposes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychosocial treatments is most likely to be effective in the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder?
questions.explanation: Of the psychosocial treatments listed, the data for effectiveness are strongest for behavior treatment, and especially for treatment with a response-inhibition component.

questions.question_text: A 7-year-old boy presents to a clinic on referral from the school with a number of behavior problems, including impaired attention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity. His parents have described him as a 'whirling dervish' for years. At age five, he was evaluated by his primary care physician and started on methylphenidate, which produced significant improvement in his behavior. However, he then developed jerky, irregular muscle movements around the eyes and mouth that persisted when he was off the medication. The medication that could address all of his symptoms is:
questions.explanation: Clonidine, an alpha-2 noradrenergic agonist, has been used successfully to treat ADHD and tic disorders and thus is the one single agent that would be most effective.

questions.question_text: A 16-year-old girl has been blinking her eyes and clearing her throat on an intermittent basis for years. She has no control of the symptoms and has never been free of them for more than a few days, and they cause significant problems. What medication may be helpful for treating this problem?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are those of Tourette's disorder. Pimozide is a frequently prescribed medication that is effective for treating Tourette's disorder.

questions.question_text: Blocking craving for opiates with subsequent reduction in associated drug use generally requires which of the following daily doses of methadone?
questions.explanation: Most patients require doses greater than 60 mg to block craving for opiates and to prevent associated drug use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most important consideration for the treatment plan when performing an initial evaluation of a patient with borderline personality disorder in suicidal crisis?
questions.explanation: Safety should be the priority. Suicidal ideation and suicide attempts are common, and it is essential during an initial assessment to decide whether inpatient treatment is necessary.

questions.question_text: The best documented treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) precipitated by a violent rape includes:
questions.explanation: Published reports by Foa and colleagues demonstrate that cognitive-based psychotherapies that facilitate destigmatization and desensitization are effective for rape victims.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old female comes to the mental health center for the first time. After a thorough assessment, she is told that the best treatment would be a course of brief psychotherapy. She looks concerned and asks if she can be transferred to a doctor of her own race. The appropriate step to take would be to:

options.text: attempt to convince her that any doctor is capable.
help her find another clinic that will suit her.
grant her request and transfer her.
explore why she feels this is necessary.

correct_answer.text: explore why she feels this is necessary.

correct_answers.text: explore why she feels this is necessary.

questions.explanation: Although the patient may ultimately be transferred to another clinician, one should still make an attempt to find out the reasoning behind her request.

questions.question_text: DSM-IV-TR cultural formulation for a patient from a culture different than the psychiatrist's requires:

options.text: an understanding of the effect of the psychiatrist's own culture on treatment variables.
a history of the patient's education and occupational training.
an understanding of the neurobiology of the patient's disorder.
independent information from a cultural consultant.

correct_answer.text: an understanding of the effect of the psychiatrist's own culture on treatment variables.

correct_answers.text: an understanding of the effect of the psychiatrist's own culture on treatment variables.

questions.explanation: According to DSM-IV-TR, the cultural formulation provides a systematic review of the individual's cultural background, the role of the cultural context in the expression and evaluation of symptoms and dysfunction, and the effect that cultural differences may have on the relationship between the individual and the clinician.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old male college student presents in the emergency department with confusion and agitation. He is distracted and talks in a rambling manner. During the interview, he reports seeing an angel who is telling him about his mission. His roommate states that the student has been having problems for months, with worsening grades, not sleeping, and withdrawal from friends. In establishing a diagnosis and preparing to initiate treatment, the most appropriate laboratory test to obtain at this point would be:

options.text: a complete blood count, including a platelet count.

questions.explanation: Substance use is a common cause of psychotic symptoms and should be eliminated before diagnosis and treatment of other psychiatric disorders.

questions.question_text: A 60-year-old woman presents with daytime fatigue, morning headache, and poor memory. Findings from her physical examination and blood studies are all within normal limits, and she reports that her mood is normal. On further questioning, she reports that her husband sleeps in a separate room because of her snoring and thrashing. The most effective treatment for this condition is:
questions.explanation: The patient likely has obstructive sleep apnea. The best treatment is continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP).

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes a characteristic of the assertive community treatment (ACT) model for management of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: In the ACT model, some level of case management is typically available round the clock, emphasizing a flexible, horizontally organized treatment team that delivers services in the community.

questions.question_text: The strong association between physical illness and suicide has been demonstrated for which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: An association between seizure disorders and increased suicide risk has been found in studies. Temporal lobe epilepsy in particular is associated with a higher suicide risk.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old man sees his primary care physician because of a recurrent productive cough. The physician recommends blood work and a chest X-ray. When the patient enters the phlebotomy suite, his heart begins to race, he perspires, and his muscles tense. When he sits in the phlebotomy chair and a tourniquet is applied, his symptoms worsen. In addition, he becomes short of breath, begins to hyperventilate, and feels numbness and tingling in his hands and feet and around his mouth. When the phlebotomist uncaps the needle, the patient passes out. He awakens shortly after an ammonia capsule is broken under his nose. He apologizes for his behavior and says, 'I always get this way when I see a needle.' This presentation is most consistent with:
questions.explanation: The essential feature of a specific phobia is marked and persistent fear of a specific object or situation. Exposure to the phobic stimulus provokes an immediate anxiety response that may appear as panic.

questions.question_text: Which symptom is significantly more likely to be associated with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) than with normal bereavement?
questions.explanation: Restricted range of affect, often called numbing, is more likely to be associated with PTSD than with normal bereavement.

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia is in the midst of a severe exacerbation but refuses treatment. The patient is able to paraphrase what the psychiatrist has said about the diagnosis, the prognosis, and the reasons for the proposed treatment with medications. Which of the following statements by the patient is the clearest example of an impaired ability to 'appreciate or understand'?

options.text: 'The space aliens living in my stomach would be injured if I took those pills.'
'Your office is bugged, but the reason why I do not want to take the medication is that I am really afraid of gaining more weight.'
'I have tried all those antipsychotics before. None of them work that well for me so why try again.'
'I am a Christian Scientist and I do not believe that I have a disease.'

correct_answer.text: 'The space aliens living in my stomach would be injured if I took those pills.'

correct_answers.text: 'The space aliens living in my stomach would be injured if I took those pills.'

questions.explanation: In option C, the patient's delusion is the causal factor impairing the appreciation standard. The appreciation standard focuses on whether the patient is able to apply facts to their own case and a delusional belief can impair appreciation if it directly causes the patient to fail to apply important facts to his or her own case.

questions.question_text: A 42-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder has responded favorably to 60 mg/day of buspirone. To avoid substantially increasing the blood level of the medication and producing side effects, you caution her to avoid regular consumption of which of the following beverages?
questions.explanation: Grapefruit juice is a potent inhibitor of intestinal CYP3A4 and may increase blood levels of buspirone when consumed regularly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following treatments has the most evidence for effectiveness in the treatment of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD)?
questions.explanation: Cognitive-behavioral therapy, particularly trauma-focused forms, has been shown to be effective in reducing symptoms of PTSD.

questions.question_text: Linkage analysis can be defined as:

options.text: an analysis that is not sensitive to a genetic model.
a study that requires the cause of the disorder to be a common risk variant.
a test to determine the chromosomal region where a disorder resides by searching for co-segregation of a genetic marker with the disorder locus.
a test to identify which of several genes in a chromosomal region is involved in the disorder in question.

correct_answer.text: a test to determine the chromosomal region where a disorder resides by searching for co-segregation of a genetic marker with the disorder locus.

correct_answers.text: a test to determine the chromosomal region where a disorder resides by searching for co-segregation of a genetic marker with the disorder locus.

questions.explanation: In linkage analysis, geneticists use genetic markers to determine the chromosomal location of the gene for a disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) who are treated with methylphenidate?

options.text: Significantly reduced risk of substance abuse in later life
Higher level of all substance abuse in adulthood

correct_answer.text: Significantly reduced risk of substance abuse in later life

correct_answers.text: Significantly reduced risk of substance abuse in later life

questions.explanation: In a long-term study, pharmacotherapy for ADHD significantly reduced the risk of substance use disorder compared to those who did not receive treatment.

questions.question_text: Elements of an individual's ability to make decisions about undergoing treatment or participating in research include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: repeating the outlined risks and benefits without prompting.
appreciating the significance of the information for the individual's own situation.
reasoning with the information or weighing options.

correct_answer.text: repeating the outlined risks and benefits without prompting.

correct_answers.text: repeating the outlined risks and benefits without prompting.

questions.explanation: An individual is not required to memorize or recite the risks and benefits of a recommended procedure without prompting to be able to make a decision.

questions.question_text: A school guidance counselor refers a 5-year-old girl who will not speak. The girl has been enrolled in school for 3 months. During this time, she has been noted to make hand gestures or nod in response to her teacher or peers. The guidance counselor has been meeting with the girl regularly, and recently the child has begun to whisper. However, she will not use a normal voice. The girl's parents report that the child has no problems speaking at home. The girl plays with her peers, makes appropriate eye contact when spoken to, seems interested in others, and has no unusual movements. There have been no delays or abnormalities in development. As an adult, this child is at high risk of developing:
questions.explanation: This young girl is suffering from selective mutism. Despite the disorder being rare, research has identified a link between selective mutism in children and social phobia in adulthood.

questions.question_text: A 10-year-old boy is brought for consultation for 'bed-wetting.' His parents report that he began using the toilet and staying dry during the day when he was 3 years old. However, he has never consistently been able to control his bladder during sleep. Physical examination and laboratory studies have demonstrated no abnormalities. His father reports that he also wet the bed as a child but stopped when he was about 12 years old. The intervention that is most likely to have long-term effectiveness with this boy is:
questions.explanation: Behavioral interventions such as the urine alarm—the 'bell and pad'—have been demonstrated to be the most effective in permanently eliminating nocturnal enuresis.

questions.question_text: A 58-year-old man has a history of ingesting 1 to 2 pints of vodka on a daily basis over the past 20 years. He presents to the emergency department after a minor motor vehicle accident and appears disorganized. A computerized tomography scan of his head is most likely to show which of the following?
questions.explanation: Chronic alcoholism is associated with cerebellar degeneration, characterized by unsteadiness of gait, problems with standing, and mild nystagmus.

questions.question_text: symptoms of obsessive compulsive disorder respond best to which of the following tricyclic antidpressants?
questions.explanation: Clomipramine, which blocks the neuronal reuptake of serotonin, improves the symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder in a manner similar to the newer SSRIs. Clomipramine was the first drug approved by the FDA for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder.

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old woman presented with a 2-week loss of difficulty sleeping, hearing voices, and problems with thinking. She was fearful and suspicious, and talked about evil alien forces out in the world. Further evaluation revealed that the woman had been raped about 3 weeks earlier. However, she has no recollection of the event. One week after initial presentation, her symptoms have disappeared and she has returned to normal functioning. The most likely diagnosis at this time is:
questions.explanation: Given the recent trauma and short duration of symptoms, brief psychotic disorder is the most reasonable diagnosis. Acute stress disorder and PTSD require the presence of avoidance, increased arousal, and reexperiencing the event. PTSD and schizophreniform disorder both require the presence of symptoms for at least 4 weeks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications is most likely to be associated with polycystic ovary syndrome?
questions.explanation: Among women who started valproate before age 20, up to 40% have polycystic ovaries.

questions.question_text: In the National Institute of Mental Health's Epidemiologic Catchment Area study, the ethnic differences in the 1-month prevalence of mental health disorders dropped after which of the following factors was controlled for?
questions.explanation: Age, socioeconomic status, and education have been confounders in various studies comparing mental illness prevalences among different races.

questions.question_text: A patient has not responded to phenelzine after 10 weeks of treatment, and a switch to fluoxetine is planned. What is the recommended minimum interval between stopping phenelzine and starting fluoxetine?
questions.explanation: Phenelzine is an irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase. Once discontinued, a period of 2 weeks is required for new enzymes to be synthesized.

questions.question_text: The single most effective treatment for major depression in elderly patients is:
questions.explanation: Remission rates for ECT are 90% or higher among elderly patients. ECT is especially indicated when an elderly patient is actively suicidal, anorexic, noncompliant with medication, or unable to tolerate medication.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old athletic man presents for evaluation of several syncopal episodes over the past month. He has been treated for hypertension during the past year and has responded nicely to 50 mg/day of metoprolol XR and 25 mg/day of hydrochlorothiazide. Three months ago his primary care physician started him on 20 mg/day of fluoxetine and 0.5 mg/day of lorazepam t.i.d. for mixed anxiety and depression. On examination the patient seems mildly anxious and demonstrates orthostatic hypotension. His ECG is unremarkable except for mild sinus bradycardia. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine is a powerful inhibitor of the cytochrome P450 2D6 isoenzyme, which metabolizes beta-blockers, including metoprolol. This can lead to increased serum levels of the beta-blocker, causing orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, and often syncope.

questions.question_text: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) appears to be most strongly associated with prenatal exposure to:
questions.explanation: Of the pharmacological agents and substances listed, the only one for which prenatal exposure has been associated with ADHD in a number of case-control studies is nicotine.

questions.question_text: Compared with Caucasian Americans, African Americans are more likely to receive a diagnosis of:
questions.explanation: Probably because of multiple factors, such as differential health care utilization patterns, differential symptom presentations, and mismatch of provider and patient race, African Americans are more likely than Caucasians to receive a diagnosis of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: The clinical sign that differentiates delirium from dementia is:
questions.explanation: Patients with dementia may exhibit psychosis, agitation, poor attention, and confusion. However, an altered or fluctuating level of consciousness is the hallmark of delirium.

questions.question_text: Gabapentin has FDA approval as an indication for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Gabapentin is approved by the Food and Drug Administration for adjunctive treatment of epilepsy and management of postherpetic neuralgia.

questions.question_text: A patient with a first episode of a nonpsychotic major depression has responded well to the acute phase medication treatment. What is the typical duration of the continuation phase?
questions.explanation: The typical duration of the continuation phase for a first episode of major depression is 4 to 9 months.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman consults a psychiatrist with a chief complaint of anxiety, insomnia with nightmares, loss of appetite, and chest pain. Tearfully, the patient reports that 2 weeks ago her husband left her for another woman. The husband told the patient, 'I need someone more adventuresome.' She suspected that her husband was having an affair, but she was unprepared for his leaving. She avoids walking by his office in their home because when she sees his litter, still on the desk, she feels chest pain. She reports fear of being alone. She continually daydreams about their life together. She can 'barely function' in her job as a hospital administrator. The most likely preliminary diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Adjustment disorder with anxiety is the best working diagnosis. The patient's loss, although painful, is not the kind of life-threatening event that acute stress and posttraumatic stress disorders require for a diagnosis.

questions.question_text: A 74-year-old man falls on an ice patch and bumps his head. During the next 4 weeks, his wife notices that he seems more forgetful and that at night he is disoriented. He also develops a persistent headache. Which of the following diagnoses is most likely to be causing this presentation?
questions.explanation: This may be a reversible dementia ccused by a chronic subdural hematoma. It frequently follows head trauma, such as those that occur in falls, when the veins of the subdural space are torn. The most common symptoms of subdural hematoma are headache, memory loss, apathy, inattention, and confusion. There can be associated hemiparesis, hemianopsia, and cranial nerve abnormalities, but these are less common.

questions.question_text: What proportion of people with dysthymic disorder experience an episode of major depression in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: Some 70%-80% of people with dysthymia have a lifetime diagnosis of major depression, and many seek treatment when they develop major depression superimposed on their dysthymia.

questions.question_text: Currently, the efficacy of a psychotherapy for treatment of a particular disorder is best judged by:

options.text: number needed to treat to number needed to harm ratio.

questions.explanation: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses along with randomized controlled trials provide level 1 evidence for treatment strategies.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old woman is diagnosed with bipolar I disorder. She has a previous history of several suicide attempts. Of the following medications, which would be the most likely to decrease her risk for suicide if administered on a long-term basis?
questions.explanation: Lithium has been shown to reduce the risk of suicidal behavior in patients with bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old man has severe panic attacks cued by public speaking. He has developed marked avoidance of such situations, which has greatly compromised his career development. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Social phobia is a marked and persistent fear of social and performance situations in which embarrassment may occur. Exposure to the social or performance situation evokes an anxiety response, which may take the form of a panic attack.

questions.question_text: A patient whose depression has responded well to an SSRI now reports symptoms of erectile dysfunction associated with the SSRI antidepressant therapy. This dysfunction has persisted for more than a month. The best initial approach would be to:

options.text: reduce the dose of the antidepressant.
continue treatment until the patient develops tolerance to the side effect.

correct_answer.text: reduce the dose of the antidepressant.

correct_answers.text: reduce the dose of the antidepressant.

questions.explanation: When a decrease in libido or a sexual dysfunction persists despite improvement in mood with an SSRI, the best approach is to attempt to lower the dose to see if the side effect will remit without loss of efficacy.
